sections.html:
Millville is a Cumberland County city where the main local rule for a seller concerns tenants. Roughly 36 percent of occupied homes are rented, so many sales involve a registered rental unit, and the city's registration and inspection code shapes what a buyer inherits.

The city has about 28,098 residents and 11,845 households. Owner occupancy is 64.1 percent, the median owner value is $219,000, and median gross rent is $1,261. With a median value that low, comparable Cumberland County sales matter more to your price than any statewide average.

Chapter 11, Article VII of the Millville code requires every residential rental unit, single family homes included, to be registered and inspected each year and again with each change in occupancy. No one may live in an unregistered unit. After a satisfactory inspection the city issues a certificate of continued occupancy, and none is issued while violations remain open.

Millville rental registration and inspection charges.
Charge or ruleAmount or terms
Annual registration and inspection$100 per unit
Paid after the due date$125 per unit
Added inspection, reinspection or cancellation with under 48 hours' notice$50 each
Registration termsAbout 25 percent of units start on each of January 1, April 1, July 1 and October 1
Exempt unitsUnits owned by the city, the Millville Housing Authority or another government agency

An owner who lives outside Cumberland County must name an agent who lives or works in the county. The lease must say it is subject to city ordinances, and at a change of occupancy the owner hands over the state Truth in Renting guide. If you are selling a tenant-occupied house, ask the Bureau of Permits and Inspections for the registration status before you list.

Millville's code spells out inspections for rental units. Call the Bureau of Permits and Inspections to ask whether a change of ownership of an owner-occupied house triggers a certificate of continued occupancy or any other inspection, and request the permit history for the address.

  • Ask whether any open permit still needs a final inspection before closing.
  • If tenants stay in place, the rental certificate and the annual inspection carry forward to the new owner.

Buyers coming from Philadelphia or the shore compare Millville on drive time and price. Workers in Millville average 25.2 minutes getting to their jobs. The city sits between the southern ends of the New Jersey Turnpike, the Garden State Parkway, Route 55 and the Atlantic City Expressway.

  • Roads: Routes 47, 49 and 55 cross the city.
  • Transit: NJ Transit bus routes 313 from Cape May to Philadelphia, 408 between Millville and Philadelphia, and 553 toward Atlantic City.
  • Local draws: the Glasstown Arts District, Wheaton Arts, the Levoy Theatre, New Jersey Motorsports Park and Laurel Lake.

The Millville Tax Collector bills on a calendar year, mails bills in mid to late July, and each bill has four stubs for August, November, February and May. The city allows a 10-day grace period, and the collector cannot honor postmarks, so a payment must arrive by the 10th. Interest is 8 percent on the first $1,500 of delinquency and 18 percent above that, with a 6 percent year-end penalty on balances over $10,000 left on June 30. Charges unpaid on the 11th day of the 11th month are delinquent and subject to the annual tax sale.

The bill schedule matters if you sell mid-year, since a stub may be due soon after the closing date and the buyer's attorney will ask who covers it. If taxes are owed when you sell, the balance is settled from your proceeds at closing, so ask the tax collector for a current figure before you accept an offer.

Cumberland County's Board of Taxation takes regular appeals from the first business day of January through April 1 at 4:00 PM, with no exceptions for lateness. In a town revalued for the current year the window runs to May 1, and added or omitted assessments can be appealed from October 1 through December 1.

The seller owes the state's Realty Transfer Fee at recording, and exemptions exist for deeds between spouses or from parent to child. A Millville deed is recorded with the Cumberland County Clerk, which keeps an office in Bridgeton and another at the Cumberland Mall. Ask the clerk's office for the current recording fee and cover sheet requirements before closing day, and ask your closing agent who files the deed and settles the transfer fee.

The pieces of a tenant sale are different from an ordinary listing, and most of the delay comes from paperwork rather than repairs. Check the registration first. Confirm with the Bureau of Permits and Inspections that the unit is registered and that the latest inspection produced a certificate of continued occupancy. Collect the signed lease, the rent roll if there are several tenants, the Truth in Renting guide handed over at the last change of occupancy, and the name of the agent if you live outside the county.

Gather the money items next. Ask the tax collector which stubs are paid and whether anything is past the 10-day grace period, because delinquent balances grow at the stated interest rates and can head toward the annual tax sale. Settle any open charges before closing so the title search comes back clean, and keep receipts for every payment you make to the city.

Plan the timeline around the inspection calendar. Registration terms start on four dates a year, so find out which one applies to your unit and avoid a lapse that leaves you paying the higher late fee. If an inspection is needed at the change of occupancy, book it as soon as a contract is signed, and give tenants the notice their lease requires so the cancellation charge for under 48 hours' notice does not apply.

Decide whether the tenants stay. Talk to them early, since occupied houses show less well and tenants who feel informed are more likely to allow inspections and showings. Nothing in the registration rules forces them out, and the new owner simply keeps the registration current. A cash buyer may take the house with tenants in place, which spares you a vacancy while you wait on a mortgage-financed buyer.

faqs.q: What does Millville charge to register a rental house?
faqs.a: $100 per unit each year, rising to $125 when paid late. A single family house that is rented counts as a unit, and added inspections or short-notice cancellations cost $50 each.

faqs.q: When is the Cumberland County appeal deadline for a Millville assessment?
faqs.a: The regular deadline is April 1 at 4:00 PM, with no exceptions for lateness. When April 1 falls on a weekend the deadline moves to the next business day, and a municipality revalued that year gets until May 1.

faqs.q: When do Millville property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Bills are due on the August, November, February and May stubs with a 10-day grace period. Charges still owed on the 11th day of the 11th month are delinquent and can go to the city's annual tax sale.

faqs.q: Do tenants have to move out before a Millville sale?
faqs.a: No rental registration rule requires it. The unit must stay registered and inspected at each change in occupancy, so the new owner must keep that registration current for anyone who stays.

faqs.q: Who pays the state transfer fee on a Millville sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it when the deed is recorded. Exemptions exist for deeds between spouses or from parent to child.
